subject: Clarify holdbacks & tiered discount on AWS private offer
messages:
From: Sophie Chen <sophie.chen@nimbus-analytics.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify holdbacks & tiered discount on AWS private offer

Hi Marcus,

Thanks for sending over the draft AWS private offer earlier this week. Our finance team is reviewing and has a couple of points we need clarified before we lock the PO:

- In the pricing sheet, there is a 12% "channel holdback" line — can you confirm whether that is retained by Redwood or passed through to the reseller?
- The tiered discount table (3 tiers) lists net revenue share at each level but we don't see an explicit cap for passback to our channel partner. Is there a minimum pass-through percentage you can commit to?
- If we commit to 2x the baseline usage for 12 months, what additional discount steps would be available and what would that mean for the reseller commission?

We're close to signing but need this clarified to get procurement sign-off. Attaching the internal summary we shared with our legal/finance leads for reference.

Thanks,

Sophie Chen
Head of Cloud Procurement
Nimbus Analytics
[attachment: nimbus_internal_summary.pdf]
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sophie Chen <sophie.chen@nimbus-analytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify holdbacks & tiered discount on AWS private offer

Sophie —

Appreciate the quick read. Short answers up front, followed by a compact breakdown attached.

1) Channel holdback: the 12% line on the draft is a retention bucket that Redwood uses to cover marketplace transaction fees + a small allocation for channel incentives in cases where a reseller is not explicit on the PO. For confirmed reseller-backed deals (e.g., you name the reseller and they appear on the Marketplace purchase flow) we will convert that line into an explicit reseller pass-through. In other words: we do not keep the full 12% if a named reseller is on the PO; we pass through at the agreed commission rate.

2) Minimum pass-through: Redwood can commit to a 7% minimum reseller pass-through for deals in this band if the reseller signs the attached distributor acknowledgement and we receive a committed minimum ARR. We outlined an example waterfall in the attached workbook (column "Reseller Pass-Through - Guaranteed").

3) Volume step-ups: for 2x baseline (12-month term) we can open an accelerated tier that increases net discounts by 200–350bps depending on whether commit is measured monthly or quarterly. In those cases, reseller commission is protected at the contract floor (7%) and we introduce an additional accelerator pool that the reseller and you can split (we usually recommend a 60/40 split in favor of the reseller to keep channel economics healthy).

I've attached private_offer_pricing_breakdown.xlsx with the waterfall examples and a sample clause to add to the PO so procurement sees the pass-through language.

If that works, confirm the reseller name and I'll prepare the updated PO with explicit pass-through and an addendum that contains the guaranteed floor and accelerator sharing.

Best,

Marcus Lin
Head of Cloud GTM, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0124
[attachment: private_offer_pricing_breakdown.xlsx]
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sophie Chen <sophie.chen@nimbus-analytics.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify holdbacks & tiered discount on AWS private offer

Marcus / Sophie —

Quick note from the channel ops side: recommend we lock the 7% floor Marcus mentioned, but add a clause that for any monthly overage above 150% of commit, the reseller gets an incremental 3% on the incremental revenue (capped at 5% incremental). This keeps the reseller motivated for growth while protecting Redwood's economics on overage.

Also suggest we add an explicit line in the PO: "Reseller identification required at purchase time to qualify for pass-through." That prevents accidental retention when the buyer purchases directly via marketplace without selecting the partner.

If you want, I can draft the short Addendum and send to Sophie for legal review.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Marketplace Partnerships | Redwood Inference
From: Sophie Chen <sophie.chen@nimbus-analytics.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 14:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify holdbacks & tiered discount on AWS private offer

Marcus / Ben —

Thanks — this clarifies things nicely. We are happy to proceed on the basis of: 1) 7% guaranteed reseller pass-through floor (reseller: CloudBridge Solutions), 2) accelerator pool split 60/40 in favor of CloudBridge for any tiered uplift, and 3) 3% incremental for overage above 150% of commit (capped at 5% incremental) as Ben suggested.

Next steps from our side: we will sign the distributor acknowledgement (attach in separate email) and route the PO to procurement if you can provide the updated PO+addendum. Can you send the DocuSign when ready?

Attaching our signed distributor_agreement template for your records.

Cheers,

Sophie Chen
Head of Cloud Procurement
Nimbus Analytics
